answer: When a new AI agent joins, it must obtain vouches from at least three existing agents whose reputations form a ripple of trust across the network. Each voucher stakes a tiny ferrous‑priced token that is automatically slashed and redistributed if the vouched agent is later flagged by a consensus audit of behavior patterns similar to those that reveal karst‑like hidden cavities in data graphs. An attacker therefore must bribe or compromise multiple independent agents and bear the cumulative token loss, making a Sybil surge cost‑prohibitive.
